title: Supported Kummer class of a principal divisor is the localization boundary of its Kummer class
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\ell$ be a prime invertible on $T$, and let $A=\mathbf F_\ell$. Let $f\in\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ be such that multiplication by $f$ on $\mathcal O_T$ is injective, so that $D=V(f)$ is an effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]; write $i:D\hookrightarrow T$ for its closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and $j:U=T\setminus D\hookrightarrow T$ for the complementary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Use the ordinary small-etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the twist $A_T(1)=\mu_{\ell,T}\otimes_{\mathbf F_{\ell,T}}A_T=\mu_{\ell,T}$ [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist], the right adjoint $Ri^!$ of $i_*$ [lem-exc-closed-ambient], and, for $K=A_T(1)$, the closed-support triangle $i_*Ri^!K\to K\to Rj_*j^*K\xrightarrow{\delta}(i_*Ri^!K)[1]$ of [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle]. Let $\kappa(f)\in H^1(U_{\mathrm{et}},\mu_\ell)=\operatorname{Hom}(A_U,j^*K[1])$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] be the image of $f|_U\in H^0(U_{\mathrm{et}},\mathbf G_m)$ under the connecting map of the exact Kummer sequence $1\to\mu_\ell\to\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{z\mapsto z^\ell}\mathbf G_m\to1$ [lem-amb-kummer-any-base], [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact]. Define $\partial\kappa(f):A_D\to Ri^!K[2]$ as the morphism corresponding, under the adjunctions $j^*\dashv Rj_*$ and $i^*\dashv i_*$ (with $i^*A_T=A_D$), to the composite $A_T\to Rj_*j^*K[1]\xrightarrow{\delta[1]}i_*Ri^!K[2]$ whose first map corresponds to $\kappa(f)$. Let $c_{D,A}:Ri_*A_D\to A_T(1)[2]$ be the supported Kummer morphism of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] with $N=\ell$, and $\eta_D:A_D\to Ri^!A_T(1)[2]$ its transpose under $i_*\dashv Ri^!$. Then there is $\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}$ with $$\eta_D=\varepsilon\,\partial\kappa(f).$$ No Noetherian, regularity or excellence hypothesis is imposed, and the sign $\varepsilon$ is not specified.

proof.text: Put $h=f|_U$. Multiplication by $f$ identifies $\mathcal O_T$ with $\mathcal I_D=(f)$; dualizing gives a global frame $e$ of $L=\mathcal O_T(D)=\mathcal I_D^\vee$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. The section obtained by transposing the ideal inclusion is $s_D=f e$. Thus the frame torsor of $L$, in the frame $e$, is $\mathbf G_m$ with specified section $h$ on $U$. This uses only the assumed injectivity of multiplication by $f$, and $h$ is invertible because $U=T-V(f)$.

proof.text: Write the group law of $G=\mathbf G_m$ additively for this extension calculation and put $Q=i_*\mathbf Z_D$. Let $e_h$ be the pushout extension of the open-closed sequence $0\to j_!\mathbf Z_U\to\mathbf Z_T\to Q\to0$ [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] along $1\mapsto h$, as in [lem-per-supported-yoneda-localization]. The adjunction $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] gives natural additive identifications $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!\mathbf Z_U,M)=M(U)$ sending the inclusion $j_!\mathbf Z_U\to\mathbf Z_T$ to the constant one; this is the hypothesis of [lem-sp-relative-torsor-extension] with $L=j_!\mathbf Z_U$ and the etale object $U$. The extension $e_{-h}$ is the sheaf quotient of $G\oplus\mathbf Z_T$ by the relations $(h(n),n)=0$ for local $n\in j_!\mathbf Z_U$, where $h(n)=nh$. The map $G\to E_{-h}$ given by $x\mapsto[(x,1)]$ is equivariant, lies over the supported generator, and sends $h$ on $U$ to zero. Hence [lem-sp-relative-torsor-extension] identifies the normalized extension of the framed line bundle in Step 1 with $e_{-h}$. The map $[(x,m)]\mapsto[(-x,m)]$ from $E_h$ to $E_{-h}$ induces $-1$ on $G$ and the identity on $Q$. Extension-class naturality [lem-sc-p1-ext-class-naturality] gives $e_{-h}=-e_h$.

proof.text: Set $K=\mu_{\ell,T}=A_T(1)$. The morphism $c=c_{D,A}$ exists by [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer]. Its defining normalization [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary] says that its abelian realization, precomposed with $Q\to i_*A_D$, is $k[1]\circ\beta$, where $k$ is the actual Kummer extension and $\beta$ is the normalized extension in Step 2. Therefore this realization is $-k[1]\circ e_h$. The Kummer sequence is exact on arbitrary $T$ because $\ell$ is invertible [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. Apply [lem-per-supported-yoneda-localization] with $G_1=\mu_\ell$, $G_2=G_3=\mathbf G_m$ and $h=f|_U$: the splice $k[1]\circ e_h$ is the supported class $\partial(\delta_U(h))=\partial\kappa(f)$. Thus the integral abelian realization of $c$ is the negative of this class, in the signed relative convention of that node.

proof.text: The preceding equality detects module morphisms, rather than merely their images after forgetting support. Indeed [lem-sp-etale-supported-integral-derived-unit], with $n=\ell$, says that $Q\to\operatorname{forget}(i_*A_D)$ is a DerivedUnit. By [def-sp-exact-functor-derived-unit], forgetting and precomposing with this generator is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T,A)}(i_*A_D,K[2])$ to $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T,\mathbf{Ab})}(Q,\operatorname{forget}K[2])$. Moreover [lem-pur-module-restriction-kernel-comparison] identifies module and abelian supported cohomology by a morphism of the three restriction-kernel complexes. Consequently it also identifies their localization connecting maps: the same chain maps on $T$ and $U$ send a relative pair $(a,b)$ to $(q_Ta,q_Ub)$, commuting with $D(a,b)=(da,\operatorname{res}(a)-db)$ and with the boundary representative $(0,-b)$ of [lem-pur-divisor-relative-cone]. Apply the bijection to Step 3 to obtain the corresponding equality of supported module morphisms via [lem-amb-closed-support-hom].

proof.text: Let $\lambda:A_T\to i_*Ri^!K[2]$ be the composite defining $\partial\kappa(f)$ before the adjunction $i^*\dashv i_*$. The supported-Hom isomorphism [lem-amb-closed-support-hom] reads its class as the localization boundary just used: the triangle of [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] has closed counit and open unit as its first two arrows, and the signed kernel-to-relative-cone model of [lem-pur-divisor-relative-cone] reads its last arrow as $(0,-b)$. Changes of cone sign affect this identification by one overall sign. Write $\beta:A_D\to Ri^!K[2]$ for the adjoint of $\lambda$ under $i^*\dashv i_*$. Then $\lambda=(i_*\beta)u_D$. Under $i_*\dashv Ri^!$ [lem-exc-closed-ambient] the corresponding supported morphism is $\operatorname{counit}_K[2]\circ i_*\beta$; this is the same supported class, since the triangle identity identifies the two adjunction descriptions. Step 4 therefore gives $c=\varepsilon(\operatorname{counit}_K[2]\circ i_*\beta)$ for $\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}$. Taking transposes gives $\eta_D=\varepsilon\beta=\varepsilon\,\partial\kappa(f)$. All inputs hold on arbitrary schemes; none imposes regularity, Noetherianity or excellence.
